fact_text: The analyst's boom-bust sequence: strong growth widens the current account deficit, devaluation then lifts dollar-linked assets, an IMF programme restores stability, and stocks rally once controls take hold.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Primary surplus means government revenue exceeds spending after excluding interest payments on public debt, so it measures the budget result before debt service.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: With a primary surplus, debt-to-GDP tends to fall over time as the economy grows relative to the debt, because the government is not adding new borrowing to cover its non-interest spending.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst named the primary surplus achieved in FY24, the first in nearly 20 years, as the main reason for that year's stock market rally.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The current account balance is driven mainly by imports, exports and workers' remittances, which bring dollars in or send them out.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Oil and LNG, whose pricing is linked to oil, make up a large share of Pakistan's imports, so a higher oil price widens the current account deficit.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: When the current account deficit is large and foreign reserves are falling, investors doubt that companies will survive to earn future profits, so the market P/E compresses.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: IMF programmes require the government to reach a primary surplus and bring the current account deficit under control.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst said that after an IMF agreement the fiscal, current account and interest rate indicators typically improve within three to six months, provided structural reforms follow.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Governments under pressure near the end of their term tend to raise subsidies and open imports to show growth, which strains reserves and deficits and often leads to a later IMF programme.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst models Pakistani politics as four players: two major parties, the courts and the military establishment. Macro stability tends to hold while they are aligned and breaks down when they split.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst said the average profit growth of about 100 listed companies was roughly 15-17% a year over the 25 years to December 2023, and that index returns track this profit growth in the long run.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Index return is roughly the growth in aggregate company profits plus the change in the market P/E multiple, and macro conditions drive that multiple up or down.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst said that over the 25 years from January 1999 to December 2023 stocks beat fixed income, gold and real estate in Pakistan, though returns came in uneven bursts with long flat stretches.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst said dollar-linked assets such as gold tend to perform strongly in phases of rupee devaluation, while stocks lag until stability returns.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A share's fair value equals the present value of the future profits and dividends it is expected to return to shareholders, discounted at the prevailing interest rate.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst, citing Warren Buffett, said interest rates act like gravity on stock prices: higher rates lower the present value of future profits and so lower fair prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: A rule of thumb for a market's fair P/E is 20 minus the long-term interest rate; the analyst found actual rates, not long-run averages, the more applicable input for Pakistan.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst said the 20-minus-rate P/E rule is reliable when interest rates sit in a normal 7-15% band and gives misleading answers at very high rates.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst said Pakistan's market is unlikely to reach a double-digit P/E while interest rates stay high, because high rates keep the fair P/E low.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's core rule is not to predict political or macro turning points but to act only once they are confirmed, accepting that the first part of the move is missed.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst cited the July 2017 disqualification of a sitting prime minister as a clear confirmation that political conditions were turning, one of his reference points for acting on the cycle.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst cited the April 2022 no-confidence vote against the sitting government as a confirmation point, after which he treated a reduction in exposure as the disciplined response.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: While macro indicators are in line and the political picture is stable, the analyst's framework keeps at least about half of a portfolio in stocks, going higher when valuations look attractive.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's framework builds a stock position in stages: a base allocation first, then additions only after returns and confirmation hold for a year or two, to limit losses if the cycle turns.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's framework aims to limit the loss from a market peak to about 10-15% by reducing exposure once confirmation arrives, rather than trying to call the top.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst's best-investment method compares each holding's expected return over a three-year horizon against a risk-free bank rate, shifting capital to other assets when prices rise too far.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst preferred fundamentally strong companies to weak cyclical ones as the more reliable bet, while acknowledging that individual weak cyclical stocks can outperform during a boom.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'INVEST LIKE A PRO - UNDERSTAND BOOM BUST CYCLES' (YouTube transcript, undated)
